title: The Expires value must be an RFC 3339 date-time

cites.quote: The value of this field is formatted according to the Internet profiles of [ISO.8601-1] and [ISO.8601-2] as defined in [RFC3339]. ... expires-field = "Expires" fs SP date-time ... date-time = < imported from Section 5.6 of [RFC3339] >
cites.note: Transcribed from a live fetch of https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9116.txt on 2026-10-29 (file sha256 79d19ce7a4a35496981095a27fd992797a9fc4d6f3649c2a1e14f494607c61f9). Lines 345-347 (§2.5.5) and the §4 ABNF. The prose sentence carries no MUST on its own; the ABNF production is the normative grammar.

policy_note: security-txt-expires-unparseable keeps the values Date cannot parse. This rule catches the values Date DOES parse but the grammar rejects: a bare date ('2027-06-20'), prose ('June 20 2027'), a space separator, a missing offset, and an impossible date Date rolls forward ('2027-02-30T00:00:00Z' parses as 2 March). The test is the RFC 3339 §5.6 grammar plus the §5.6/§5.7 part ranges (month 01-12, day within its month, hour 00-23, minute 00-59, second 00-60, offset hour 00-23 and minute 00-59). 'T' and 'Z' match case-insensitively: RFC 3339 §5.6 allows lowercase, and erratum EID 7264 (uppercase Z only) is Reported, not Verified. When this rule fires, the expiry age rules (expired, expiring-soon, expires-over-a-year) are skipped, as sectxt does. A value outside the grammar may lack an offset, and Date reads some such values in the runner's local time zone ('June 20 2027'); Date also rolls an impossible date forward. An age computed from such a value is not trustworthy. A grammatical leap second (second 60) is read as second 59, because Date refuses second 60; it is neither unparseable nor a format finding.
applicability: A security.txt body whose first Expires value Date parses.
expectation: The first Expires value matches /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})[Tt](\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})(?:\.\d+)?(?:[Zz]|[+-](\d{2}):(\d{2}))$/ and each part is in its RFC 3339 range.

cases.name: 30 February, which Date rolls forward to 2 March
lowercase t, a fraction and a numeric offset
lowercase t and z, as the RFC 9116 §2.5.5 example writes
Date cannot parse it -- security-txt-expires-unparseable fires instead
